opps.name: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSMC)
opps.why: TSMC's Q3 revenue rose 41% to $46.72bn, beating its own guidance, and it guided Q4 to $52.3bn to $54.3bn, about 14% higher quarter on quarter, with management calling AI demand extremely robust. Yet the US-listed shares fell as much as 5.3% and closed 1.8% lower in the AI sell-off, so strong results are not being rewarded.
opps.positives: Record profit up 69% and ahead of consensus; Q4 revenue guide above expectations; 2026 revenue growth now seen near 44%; AI demand broadening into CPUs and networking chips
opps.negatives: Gross margin guided slightly lower on 2nm ramp and overseas fabs; AI financing scare (CoreWeave) could hit customer spending; Fed hike risk weighs on tech valuations; Taiwan geopolitical risk
opps.source_title: MT Newswires via Bigdata.com: TSMC quarterly profit surges 69% to record
opps.thesis: Long TSMC: AI demand is driving revenue about 14% higher next quarter, so the shares should recover the post-results dip once the AI financing scare fades.
opps.stop_trigger: Exit if TSMC cuts guidance or a major hyperscaler announces lower AI capex

opps.name: Persimmon
opps.why: Persimmon rose 2.8% on 14 Oct after the Bank of England's chief economist doubted the four rate rises priced by markets, and gilt yields have eased from their 19-year high. The Budget on 28 Oct is expected to detail a first-time buyer scheme that RBC called the catalyst the sector needed.
opps.positives: Gilt yields retreating from multi-year highs; BoE chief economist sceptical of aggressive hikes; First Homes scheme due in the Budget; sector valuations still near post mini-budget lows
opps.negatives: Bellway warned higher mortgage rates are constraining demand; earlier pre-Budget gains were wiped out once; a poorly received Budget could push gilt yields back up
opps.source_title: Alliance News via Bigdata.com: FTSE 100 closes higher despite hot US inflation
opps.thesis: Long Persimmon: UK housebuilder valuations sit at post mini-budget lows, so easing gilt yields plus a Budget first-time buyer scheme should re-rate the shares.
opps.stop_trigger: Exit if the 10-year gilt yield breaks back above its October high or the Budget disappoints on housing

opps.name: Micron Technology
opps.why: Micron rose 1.9% on Thursday while the wider chip index fell, and Korea's memory giants bounced more than 4% on Friday. KeyBanc still expects DRAM prices to rise 15% to 20% a year in Q4, and industry voices call the CXMT claim unverified, with scaling unlikely before 2028.
opps.positives: Relative strength returning; DRAM and NAND price forecasts still rising; high-bandwidth memory pricing could jump in early 2027; CXMT is weakest in the most profitable segment
opps.negatives: CXMT now holds roughly 10% of DRAM and is growing; chip index on a seven-day losing run; Fed hike risk weighs on tech; very volatile after a 191% year-to-date gain
opps.source_title: Globe and Mail via Bigdata.com: Why is Micron stock still dropping?
opps.thesis: Long Micron: the memory sell-off is driven by an unverified Chinese DRAM claim while AI-led demand and rising memory prices remain intact.
opps.stop_trigger: Exit if CXMT's claim is independently verified at scale or DRAM contract prices start falling

opps.name: Valero Energy
opps.why: Brokers including Goldman Sachs, UBS and Barclays have lifted Valero targets into the $400 to $450 range on wider diesel margins and record buybacks. The IEA is releasing only around 20m barrels of diesel from reserves, well short of the 50m some expected, so the squeeze persists, but the shares have already run about 7x in five years.
opps.positives: Diesel shortage seen lasting into 2027; reserve release smaller than feared; brokers forecasting about $4bn of quarterly buybacks; Q3 results next week
opps.negatives: Valuation now looks full after a near-record high; a US-Iran deal could collapse the risk premium; heating oil down 12% in a month; political risk of windfall measures
opps.source_title: Yahoo Finance via Bigdata.com: Valero fair value rises after analysts lift margin outlook
opps.thesis: Long Valero: record diesel margins from war-damaged refining capacity should flow into Q3 and Q4 earnings and buybacks while the squeeze lasts into 2027.
opps.stop_trigger: Exit on a US-Iran agreement that restores Gulf flows, or a sharp fall in diesel margins

opps.name: Roper Technologies
opps.why: Roper has beaten earnings estimates by an average of 2.8% over the last two quarters and screens for another beat when it reports Q3 on 22 Oct. It is a low-volatility, cash-generative software compounder in a market rotating away from expensive tech.
opps.positives: Recurring revenue and strong cash conversion; consistent earnings beats; low volatility suits the defensive rotation; new board member with AI transformation experience
opps.negatives: Model fair value gaps can persist; software multiples pressured by AI disruption fears and high yields; acquisition-led growth is sensitive to borrowing costs
opps.source_title: Nasdaq via Bigdata.com: Why Roper is poised to beat earnings estimates again
opps.thesis: Long Roper: a high-quality software compounder trading below fair value, with a Q3 beat likely to start closing the gap.
opps.stop_trigger: Exit if Q3 shows organic growth slowing or guidance is cut

opps.name: Albemarle
opps.why: Mizuho's upgrade argues demand from grid battery storage has tipped lithium into a more favourable balance and sees lithium carbonate rising to $22,500 a tonne by end 2027. But earnings estimates are still being cut, with one quant ranking it a strong sell, so Q3 results on 5 Nov are the test.
opps.positives: Lowest-cost lithium producer; storage demand ahead of expectations; new supply constrained by long lead times; 15 of 23 analysts rate it a buy
opps.negatives: Shares down 31% this year; earnings estimates still falling; lithium prices volatile; higher rates can slow battery and EV demand
opps.source_title: CNBC Pro via Bigdata.com: A recovery in lithium demand will drive this stock higher, Mizuho says
opps.thesis: Long Albemarle: storage-led lithium demand is tightening the market before prices or estimates reflect it.
opps.stop_trigger: Exit if Q3 results show lithium pricing still falling

opps.name: Bank of America
opps.why: The dip is no longer just the one-off fine: Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.08 missed the $1.11 consensus and revenue of $29.96bn fell short by about $0.7bn as trading and advisory fees disappointed. Morgan Stanley still rates it Overweight on 2027 interest income but cut its target to $61 from $67.
opps.positives: Penalty is quantified and settled; consumer and wealth units grew profits; Morgan Stanley sees positive operating leverage in 2027; financials rose on Thursday
opps.negatives: Core revenue miss, not just the fine; trading down 5% and investment banking fees down 11%; political criticism of the fine; slowing economy raises credit losses
opps.source_title: Benzinga via Bigdata.com: Bank of America analysts slash forecasts after weak Q3
opps.thesis: Long Bank of America: a quantified penalty created a dip, and rising net interest income should drive earnings growth into 2027.
opps.stop_trigger: Exit if regulators widen the probe, credit losses rise or more brokers cut targets

opps.name: Burberry
opps.why: Frasers Group lifted its position to 7.42% from 6.32%, its second increase in a fortnight, as Burberry's turnaround starts to show progress. The exposure is held through sold put options expiring October 2026, March 2027 and September 2027, not direct shares, so it is a bet rather than a confirmed approach.
opps.positives: Strategic investor adding twice in two weeks; turnaround focus on core trench coats and scarves; Frasers already owns Harvey Nichols and holds Hugo Boss
opps.negatives: Position held via put options, not shares; no bid announced; luxury demand weak in a high-inflation, high-rate world; October put expiry could unwind interest
opps.source_title: MT Newswires via Bigdata.com: Frasers Group's shareholding in Burberry rises to 7.4%
opps.thesis: Watch Burberry: a strategic investor is building exposure, which can come before a bid, but nothing is announced.
opps.stop_trigger: Exit if Frasers stops adding or lets its October puts lapse without converting

opps.name: Moderna
opps.why: Moderna rose 5.3% on Thursday as money rotated from AI into healthcare, extending a run built on its personalised cancer vaccine with Merck. Phase 3 melanoma results will be presented at the ESMO Presidential Symposium on 24 Oct, a binary event for the shares.
opps.positives: Earlier data showed delayed melanoma recurrence; newly added to the Nasdaq-100; healthcare is the market's strongest sector this month; NIH-backed cancer vaccine campaign planned
opps.negatives: Binary outcome: weak data would reverse the run; shares have already moved ahead of the data; core vaccine sales still under pressure
opps.source_title: Benzinga via Bigdata.com: Nike, Moderna, Walmart get a lift as traders flee AI stocks
opps.thesis: Watch Moderna: positive Phase 3 melanoma data at ESMO on 24 Oct would validate its cancer vaccine platform and re-rate the shares; weak data would reverse the run.
opps.stop_trigger: Avoid or exit if the ESMO Phase 3 data disappoint

opps.name: CoreWeave
opps.why: Flagged as a danger, not an opportunity. Credit default swap spreads hit 1,140 basis points, a level S&P Global calls distressed, and its 2031 bond yields 15.8%; the shares have lost a third in seven sessions. Even bullish BofA forecasts about $67bn of negative free cash flow from 2026 to 2028.
opps.positives: Nvidia's CEO publicly backed it; BofA keeps a Buy with a $140 target; prepayments of around 50% on many contracts
opps.negatives: Distressed credit pricing worsening week on week; interest cover of 0.3x expected for 2026; heavy new borrowing needed as rates rise; contagion risk to other neoclouds
opps.source_title: CNBC via Bigdata.com: CoreWeave credit default swaps hit distress levels
opps.thesis: Avoid CoreWeave: distressed bond pricing and heavy debt into rising rates make dips dangerous.
opps.stop_trigger: Revisit only if CDS spreads fall back below 1,000 bps and refinancing is secured

note.top_title: TSMC's beat is being ignored: pick of the day
note.top_call: Our pick of the day is Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM), radar score 68, base case +14%. TSMC beat its own Q3 guidance and guided Q4 revenue about 14% higher, yet the US shares closed 1.8% lower as the AI financing scare around CoreWeave spread. Good news ignored by a fearful market is the setup we want, with the 28 Oct Fed meeting the main risk.
note.developments: US PPI jumped 1.3% in September, the most since March 2022, after CPI hit 3.7%, and a December Fed hike is now priced above 90%; Treasury yields eased to 5.08% and the Dow rose 1.1%, with healthcare leading and tech lagging; MSCI's proposal to cut Indonesia to standalone status sent the Jakarta index down over 10%; CoreWeave credit spreads hit distress levels, strengthening our Avoid call; Micron thesis now Strengthening as memory stocks bounced and the Kospi rose 4%, while Bank of America moves to Weakening after a core revenue miss; no watchlist triggers were met, so no promotions today
note.events: 16 Oct: Fed Chair Warsh and BoE Governor Bailey speak; 21 Oct: UK CPI for September; 22 Oct: Valero and Roper Q3 results; 24 Oct: Moderna Phase 3 melanoma data at ESMO; 28 Oct: UK Budget and Fed decision
note.trade: Long TSMC on the post-results dip as AI demand accelerates; wrong if TSMC trims guidance or a major hyperscaler cuts AI capex, or if the Fed hikes on 28 Oct and tech sells off again.
note.source_title: MT Newswires via Bigdata.com: TSMC quarterly profit surges 69% to record
